questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Real-world cross-cloud serverless platforms demand automated image signing and artifact attestations. This question tests end-to-end workflow design, policy enforcement decisions, and practical CI/CD integration skills.

## Key Concepts

- Cosign signing and verification
- Rekor attestations for transparency and auditability
- SBOM generation (using tools like Syft)
- Multi-cloud serverless deployment patterns
- GitHub Actions workflow integration

## Code Example

```yaml
name: cks-serverless-sign
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize]

jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Install cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3

      - name: Set up Syft for SBOM
        uses: anchore/syft-action@v1

      - name: Build and push image
        run: |
          docker build -t ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }} .
          docker push ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }}

      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: |
          syft ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }} -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.json

      - name: Sign image with cosign
        run: |
          cosign sign --key cosign.key ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }}

      - name: Verify signature
        run: |
          cosign verify --key cosign.pub ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }}

      - name: Upload to Rekor
        run: |
          cosign upload blob -f attestation.json
```

## Failing Manifest (Unsigned Image)

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: serverless-workload
spec:
  containers:
  - name: function
    image: registry.example.com/serverless-fn:abc123
```

## Passing Manifest (Signed Image)

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: serverless-workload
spec:
  containers:
  - name: function
    image: registry.example.com/serverless-fn:signed-sha256
    imagePullPolicy: Always
```

## Local Verification

```bash
# Verify image signature
cosign verify --key cosign.pub registry.example.com/serverless-fn:signed-sha256

# Verify attestation
cosign verify-attestation --type cyclonedx --key cosign.pub registry.example.com/serverless-fn:signed-sha256
```

## CI Verification Steps

1. Add Cosign verification step in CI pipeline
2. Block deployment if signature verification fails
3. Verify SBOM matches image contents
4. Check Rekor transparency log for attestation

## Why This Is Asked

This question tests practical security controls: CI image signing, tag governance, and runtime enforcement with Kyverno; it requires understanding Cosign, Rekor, image verification, and policy-as-code interplay, plus how to craft minimal manifests and verify locally, in CI, and at runtime.

## Key Concepts

- Cosign signing and verification
- Tag policy regex
- Kyverno image verification at admission
- Minimal manifest testing (unsigned vs signed)
- CI and runtime integration and trade-offs (latency, private registries)

## Code Example

```yaml

name: CI Image Sign Check
on: pull_request
jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v1
      - name: Verify signatures
        run: |
          cosign verify registry.example.com/ride-service:1.0.0
```

```yaml

apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: require-signed-images
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
  - name: verify-signed-image
    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["Deployment"]
    validateImages:
      - image: "*"
        cosign:
          publicKey: |
            -----BEGIN PUBLIC KEY-----
            ...
            -----END PUBLIC KEY-----
```

  name: ride-service

      containers:

        image: registry.example.com/ride-service:1.0.0-signed

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to create simple, deterministic CI gates focused on security hygiene in manifests, with minimal tooling. Shows understanding of Kubernetes volumes, YAML parsing, and CI integration.

## Key Concepts

- Kubernetes hostPath security risks
- Manifest scanning with lightweight parsers (yq, Python)
- GitHub Actions workflow basics
- Local verification of a detector script

## Code Example

```python
# detector.py
import sys, yaml
def has_hostpath(path):
  data = yaml.safe_load(open(path))
  vols = data.get('spec', {}).get('volumes', []) or []
  for v in vols:
    if 'hostPath' in v:
      return True
  return False
if __name__ == '__main__':
  ok = True
  for f in sys.argv[1:]:
    if has_hostpath(f):
      ok = False
      print('HOSTPATH found in', f)
  sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)
```

## Follow-up Questions

## Why This Is Asked
Gauges practical multi-language CI in a monorepo by targeting only changed services, highlighting test coverage enforcement and per-service reporting.

### Key Concepts
- Detect changed services with git diff filtered by language folders
- Language-specific test commands and coverage collection
- Aggregate results and fail-fast if any service falls below threshold

### Code Example
```yaml
name: PR Gate: Changed Services Tests
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [ main, master ]
jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v3
        with:
          node-version: '18'
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v4
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'
      - id: changed
        run: |
          CHANGED=$(git diff --name-only ${{ github.event.before }} ${{ github.sha }} | sed -E 's|/.*$||' | sort -u)
          echo "changed=$CHANGED" > changed.txt
          echo "services=$CHANGED" >> changed.txt
      - name: Run tests for changed services
        if: always()
        run: |
          for s in ${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}/services/*; do
            dir=$(basename "$s")
            if [ -f "services/$dir/package.json" ]; then
              echo "Testing Node service: $dir"
              (cd services/$dir && npm ci && npm test -- --coverage)
            fi
            if [ -f "services/$dir/requirements.txt" ]; then
              echo "Testing Python service: $dir"
              (cd services/$dir && python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt && pytest --maxfail=1 --disable-warnings --cov=. --cov-report=xml && deactivate)
            fi
          done
      - name: Enforce coverage
        run: |
          echo "Coverage checks would be parsed here; fail if any < 75% per service"
```

- Add per-service summary artifacts for reviews

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: enforce-ml-provenance
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Fail
  rules:
  - name: require-provenance-annotations
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Deployment
    validate:
      message: 'Missing provenance annotations: model_version, dataset_hash, training_run_id'
      pattern:
        metadata:
          annotations:
            model_version: '*'
            dataset_hash: '*'
            training_run_id: '*'
  - name: require-image-digest
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Deployment
    validate:
      message: 'Container image must include a digest'
      pattern:
        spec:
          template:
            spec:
              containers:
              - image: '*@*'
```

```yaml

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment

  name: ml-inference-fail
  annotations:
    model_version: v1
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: ml
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: predictor
        image: registry.internal/ml/predictor:latest
```

```yaml
# Passing Deployment (with provenance and digest)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: ml-inference-pass
  annotations:
    model_version: v1.2.3
    dataset_hash: sha256:abcdef1234567890
    training_run_id: tr-789
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: ml
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: predictor
        image: registry.internal/ml/predictor@sha256:12345abcdef
```
